The page had zero id attributes before this edit (census: mdn=0 ids=0 pre=1 tables=3); no code block was added because the page already ships one <pre><code> example. KIND: web-api, not css - the inventoried surface is seven script methods on Element and Window and their Promise return values, even though the page's eyebrow tags it css and its spec home is CSSOM View. SOURCE KINDS: the ChromeStatus record is browser-data; issue #1562 is recorded as other because it is the record's spec_link and carries the 2018-05-16 CSSWG resolution, but it is a working-group discussion thread rather than normative text. The normative IDL (drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view) and the promisify-scroll explainer are NOT linked from the page, so they cannot be contract sources here - the validator requires every cited source URL to be linked from the target page. NOT-APPLICABLE DIMENSIONS (missing is forbidden, so each gap is named instead): inputs x7 - the page gives the call form but never documents the ScrollToOptions/ScrollIntoViewOptions members, types, defaults or validation; securityPrivacy x7 - the page carries no security or privacy content at all and the cited record marks both reviews "Not applicable". CONTEXT MAPPED, WITH A RECORDED GAP: context is documented at #syntax because that table qualifies every method with its receiver interface (Element. / Window.); the page states no exposure, secure-context, permission or other prerequisite surface. ERRORS MAPPED, WITH A CAVEAT: errors is documented at #why-it-exists because that fragment is where the page states a rejection path; the sentence itself ("A rejected Promise indicates an error (e.g. element was removed)") is reported to the implementer as a DIVERGENCE from the cited sources and is NOT adjudicated or rewritten here. Two further divergences (the resolved value, and the two-argument overloads' return type) plus a stale Safari cell are likewise drafted in the unit report rather than written into the page. NO outOfScope ARRAY, DELIBERATELY: the page's #syntax section is a table, not an IDL <pre> block, so declaredSurfaceMembers() is empty and validateDeclaredSurface() errors on ANY outOfScope name ("matches no member declared in the page's syntax block"). The real IDL surface is wider than the inventoried seven options-object call signatures - Element carries seven overloads (including scrollIntoView's `boolean or ScrollIntoViewOptions` argument) and Window six, because each of scroll/scrollTo/scrollBy also takes (x, y) - and those two-argument overloads are NOT inventoried: the page's only statement about them is the sentence reported as a divergence, so mapping documented dimensions onto it would certify a claim this unit believes the cited sources contradict. That gap is recorded here rather than papered over with an inventory entry.
